Attorney General for India - R Venkatramani, who became the 16th Attorney General on 1st October 2022. The Attorney General is appointed by the President of India and is the chief legal advisor to the Government.

Solicitor General of India - Tushar Mehta. The Solicitor General is the second-highest law officer of the country, subordinate to the Attorney General, and assists in fulfilling official legal responsibilities.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India is Girish Chandra Murmu (former Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir).
Principal Director General of Press Information Bureau is Satyendra Prakash.

Director of Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) is Ravi Sinha.
National Security Advisor of India is Ajit Doval.
Central Vigilance Commissioner of India is P K Srivastava.
Chief Economic Advisor of India is V Anantha Nageshwaran.

NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1st January 2015. It is the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India. CEO - BVR Subrahmanyam; Vice Chairperson - Suman Bery.

Chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission of India - Justice (Retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari (April 2025–Incumbent). The Commission advises the Government of India on legal reform and is headed by a retired judge.
The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31st December 2023 for the period 2026–2031, with recommendations applying from 1 April 2026. Chairman - Arvind Panagariya.

The Finance Commission is a constitutional body set up under Article 280 of the Constitution of India. It recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and States and is constituted by the President every 5 years.
The 16th Finance Commission retains the states' tax share at 41% and introduces a new weight for contribution to GDP among its devolution criteria.
NHRC Chairperson - Arun Kumar Mishra. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), established in 1993, is an independent statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
EXIM Bank (Export-Import Bank of India) Managing Director - Ms Harsha Bangari. EXIM Bank is India's leading export financing institution headquartered in Mumbai.

The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the President of India in collaboration with the Election Commission to redraw constituency boundaries based on the latest census. Its decisions have the force of law and cannot be challenged in court.
US Treasury Secretary is Scott Bessent (2025–Present).
European Parliament President – Roberta Metsola; European Council President – António Costa; European Commission President – Ursula von der Leyen.
First Governor General of Bengal is Warren Hastings.
First Governor General of British India is William Bentinck.
Only Indian and the last Governor General of India is C Rajagopalachari (also known as Rajaji).
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun because the name Japan (Nihon) means 'where the sun rises'.
Arunachal Pradesh is called the Land of the Rising Sun in the Indian context, as it is the first state in India to witness sunrise.
The Brahmaputra river is called the Sorrow of Assam due to its devastating annual floods. The same river is known as Tsangpo in China.
Andhra Pradesh is called the Rice Bowl of India due to its high production of rice.
The National Emergency in India has been declared three times — in 1962 during the India-China war, in 1971 during the Indo-Pakistan war, and from 1975 to 1977 under Indira Gandhi's government.
The three types of emergencies in India are: National Emergency (Article 352), President's Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).

India's first Prime Minister was Jawaharlal Nehru. Notable PMs include Lal Bahadur Shastri (Man of Peace), Indira Gandhi (only woman PM), P V Narasimha Rao (first South Indian PM), and Manmohan Singh (first Sikh PM).
The Siliguri Corridor, also known as the Chicken's Neck, is a stretch of land 20–22 km wide in West Bengal that connects the eight northeastern states to the rest of India.

Individual Satyagraha (1940–41) was initiated by Mahatma Gandhi to assert the right to free speech against the war effort. Vinoba Bhave was chosen as the first Satyagrahi, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru.
The First Island Chain comprises the Kuril Islands, the Japanese Archipelago, Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, the northwest Philippines, and Borneo.
India's major stock exchange indices are the BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) and NSE (National Stock Exchange).
USA's major stock exchange indices are NASDAQ, S&P 500, Dow Jones, and NYSE (New York Stock Exchange).
London's stock exchange index is the FTSE (Financial Times Stock Exchange), commonly known as The Footsie.
China's major stock exchanges are the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Japan's stock exchange index is the Nikkei 225 (Nikkei Stock Average).
South Korea's stock exchange index is the KOSPI (Korea Composite Stock Price Index).
France's stock exchange index is the CAC 40 (Cotation Assistée en Continu).
Germany's stock exchange index is the DAX (Deutscher Aktienindex).
India is Rupee; US - Dollar; UK - Pound Sterling; Europe - Euro; Russia - Ruble.
China is Renminbi (Yuan); Japan - Yen; South Korea - Korean Won; Indonesia - Indonesian Rupiah.
Malaysia is Ringgit; Thailand - Thai Baht; Vietnam - Vietnamese Dong; Bangladesh - Taka.
Pakistan is Pakistani Rupee; Nepal - Nepalese Rupee; Bhutan - Ngultrum; Maldives - Maldivian Rufiyaa.
Brazil is Brazilian Real; Argentina - Peso; South Africa - Rand.

MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act), launched in 2005, is one of the largest work guarantee programmes in the world. It guarantees 100 days of paid employment per financial year to adult members of rural households willing to do unskilled manual work.
As of 2022–23, there are 15.4 crore active workers under the MGNREGA scheme.

The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission-Gramin (VBG RAM-G) Act, 2025 is a major overhaul of MGNREGA, increasing guaranteed work from 100 to 125 days and raising the minimum daily wage to Rs 240.
VBG RAM-G mandates that at least one-third of beneficiaries must be women, and guarantees rural adults work within 15 days of demand, failing which an unemployment allowance must be given.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is the Indian government's flagship programme for financial inclusion, aiming to expand access to bank accounts, remittances, credit, insurance, and pensions.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana is the Indian government's programme to provide housing for all, targeting urban and rural poor households.
Make in India is the Indian government's initiative to promote the manufacturing of electronic goods and other products within India.
Ayushman Bharat (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana) is the Indian government's programme to provide affordable and quality healthcare to the rural and economically weaker population.
Start-up India is the Indian government's initiative to promote entrepreneurship and start-up culture across the country.
Digital India is the Indian government's programme to promote digital literacy, digital infrastructure, and digital services across the country.
The Saubhagya Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) is an Indian government project aimed at providing electricity connections to all households.

PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Aatmanirbhar Nidhi) is a micro-credit scheme launched in 2020 offering collateral-free loans of ₹10,000 to street vendors, with subsequent loans of ₹20,000 and ₹50,000, at 7% interest subsidy. The implementation body is SIDBI.

UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is an instant real-time payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). In December 2022, UPI crossed 7.82 billion transactions worth Rs 12.82 trillion.

MSME classification in India: Micro — investment up to Rs 1 crore and turnover up to Rs 5 crore; Small — investment up to Rs 10 crore and turnover up to Rs 50 crore; Medium — investment up to Rs 50 crore and turnover up to Rs 250 crore.

SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) is the apex regulatory body for licensing and regulation of MSME finance companies in India, under the Ministry of Finance, headquartered in Lucknow.

SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the regulatory body for securities and commodity markets in India. The current (11th) Chairperson is Tuhin Kanta Pandey, who took office on March 1, 2025.
January 9 - Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, commemorating Mahatma Gandhi's return from South Africa to Mumbai on 9 January 1915.
January 12 - National Youth Day (Vivekananda Jayanti), the birthday of Swami Vivekananda.
January 15 - Army Day, marking Field Marshal K M Cariappa's taking over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army from General Francis Roy Bucher on 15 January 1949.
January 16 is National Startup Day.
January 23 - Parakram Diwas / Netaji Jayanti, marking the birthday of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
January 26 - Republic Day, commemorating the Constitution of India coming into effect on 26 January 1950.
January 30 - Martyr's Day / Shaheed Diwas, the death anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
February 28 - National Science Day, marking the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir CV Raman on 28 February 1928, for which he won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
March 3 - World Wildlife Day, the birthday of CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora), signed in 1973.
March 8 is International Women's Day.
March 23 - World Meteorological Day, commemorating the creation of the World Meteorological Organization on 23 March 1950.
April 7 is World Health Day; April 14 - Ambedkar Jayanti; April 18 - World Heritage Day; April 22 - World Earth Day.
April 23 - World Book Day. UNESCO's World Book Capital for 2026 is Rabat, Morocco.
May 1 is International Workers Day / Labour Day; May 3 - International Press Freedom Day.
May 8 - World Red Cross Day / Red Crescent Day, the birth anniversary of Jean-Henry Dunant, co-founder of the Red Cross.
May 22 is International Biodiversity Day; June 5 - World Environment Day; June 21 - International Yoga Day.
July 1 - National Doctor's Day, in memory of Dr Bidhan Chandra Roy, former Chief Minister of West Bengal.
July 18 - Nelson Mandela International Day; July 22 - National Flag Day, commemorating the adoption of the Indian Tricolour on 22 July 1947.
August 12 is International Youth Day; August 15 - Independence Day; August 20 - Sadbhavana Diwas (birth anniversary of Rajiv Gandhi).
August 29 - National Sports Day, the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.
September 5 - Teacher's Day, the birth anniversary of Dr Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan — first VP, second President of India, and Bharat Ratna awardee.
September 16 is World Ozone Day; September 25 - Antyodaya Diwas (in honour of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya); September 27 - World Tourism Day.
October 2 is Gandhi Jayanti / International Day for Non-Violence; October 8 - Indian Air Force Day; October 16 - International Food Day (founding of UN-FAO).
November 14 - Children's Day, the birth anniversary of India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
December 1 is World AIDS Day; December 4 - Indian Navy Day; December 10 - World Human Rights Day.
December 16 - Vijay Diwas, observing India's victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Indo-Pak war.
December 23 - Farmer's Day / Kisan Diwas; December 26 - Veer Baal Diwas, paying homage to the four sons (Sahibzades) of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.
NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration; ISRO is the Indian Space Research Organisation; DRDO is the Defence Research and Development Organisation.
The global space economy was estimated at $450 billion in 2020 and expected to reach $600 billion by 2025. India's space economy was $9.6 billion in 2020 and is expected to reach $13 billion by 2025.
The closest large galaxy to the Milky Way is the Andromeda Galaxy, also known as Messier 31 or M31, approximately 2.5 million light years from Earth.

The closest gravitationally bound star system to us is Alpha Centauri, which has three stars: Alpha Centauri A, Alpha Centauri B, and Proxima Centauri — the closest individual star to the Sun at about 4 light years away.
The universe is constantly expanding, as discovered by Edwin Hubble and others in the 1920s. The Hubble constant describes the rate of expansion at different distances from a point in space.
The James Webb Space Telescope, developed by NASA, is 100 times more powerful than the Hubble Telescope. It sent back its first deep infrared images of the universe and Jupiter on July 12, 2022.
The Wisdom teeth are the third molar teeth, typically the last to emerge in adulthood.
NASA's Venus mission DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble Gases, Chemistry and Imagery) is planned to launch in 2029.
A Kilonova is a transient astronomical event that occurs when two neutron stars, or a neutron star and a black hole, merge in a compact binary system.
A Supernova is the cataclysmic explosion of a massive star at the end of its life, during which the star may reach maximum brightness before collapsing.

Earth's gravitational wave detectors include LIGO (USA), KAGRA (Japan), and VIRGO (Europe). Space-based missions LISA, TAIJI, and D-ECIGO will probe gravitational waves from orbit. LIGO-India is also planned.

Most abundant element in the Universe - Hydrogen (followed by Helium); Most abundant element in Earth's crust - Oxygen; Most abundant metal in Earth's crust - Aluminium; Most abundant gas in the Atmosphere - Nitrogen.

Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto using the Lowell Telescope. Pluto was the first object identified in what is now known as the Kuiper Belt — a doughnut-shaped ring of icy objects beyond Neptune, from about 30 to 55 AU.

The largest moon in the solar system is Ganymede (moon of Jupiter, 5262 km). The second largest is Titan (moon of Saturn, 5150 km). Our Moon is the fifth largest at 3475 km. The largest moon of Neptune is Triton.

The Kessler Syndrome, proposed by NASA scientist Donald J Kessler in 1978, describes a scenario where Earth's orbit becomes so crowded with debris that collisions create more debris in a self-sustaining cascade, making certain orbits unusable.

Project NETRA (Network for Space Objects Tracking and Analysis) is India's early warning system for tracking debris and hazards to Indian satellites. It can spot objects as small as 10 cm up to a range of 3,400 km.
ISRO's EOS-06 satellite observes ocean colour data, sea surface temperature, and wind vector data for oceanography and meteorological applications.

The Piezoelectric Effect is the ability of certain materials — such as quartz, ceramics, and some crystals — to generate an electric charge in response to applied mechanical stress. It is used in sensors, actuators, and energy harvesting devices.
Scientists spotted the piezoelectric effect in liquids for the first time, challenging 143 years of theory that the effect occurs only in solids.

NASA's Dragonfly mission will explore Titan, Saturn's largest moon, using an eight-rotor drone-like vehicle. It is scheduled for launch in 2027 and expected to arrive at Titan around 2034 to search for signs of life.

Artemis 1, completed on 11 December 2022, was an uncrewed test flight that circled the Moon. It tested the Space Launch System (SLS), the most powerful rocket ever built, generating 8.8 million pounds of thrust.

Artemis 2 is a crewed mission planned to carry four astronauts — Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen — on a lunar flyby, taking humans further than ever before.
Artemis 3 will be the first crewed Moon landing since Apollo 17 in 1972, with the goal of landing the first woman and first person of colour on the lunar surface.

Graphene is extracted from graphite and is made of pure carbon. It is the thinnest, most electrically and thermally conductive material in the world — 200 times stronger than steel but six times lighter. It is often called a wonder material.
Graphene exhibits giant magnetoresistance (GMR) at room temperatures — a property where electrical resistance is affected by magnetic fields in adjacent materials.
The Nobel Prize ceremonies for Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Economic Sciences are held in Stockholm, Sweden. The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
Nobel Prize for Chemistry 2022 - Carolyn R Bertozzi, Morten Meldal, and K Barry Sharpless for the development of Click Chemistry and Bioorthogonal Chemistry.
Nobel Prize for Physics 2022 - Alain Aspect, John F Clauser, and Anton Zeilinger for experiments with entangled photons establishing the violation of Bell inequalities.
Nobel Prize for Physiology/Medicine 2022 - Svante Pääbo, for discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution.
Nobel Prize for Economic Sciences 2022 - Ben S Bernanke, Douglas W Diamond, and Philip H Dybvig, for research on banks and financial crises.
Nobel Prize in Literature 2022 - Annie Ernaux; Nobel Peace Prize 2022 - Ales Bialiatski, Russian human rights organisation Memorial, and Ukrainian org Centre for Civil Liberties.
First Indian to win a Nobel Prize for Science - Sir CV Raman, Nobel Prize in Physics 1930, for the discovery of the Raman Effect.
John Bardeen is the only person to win the Nobel Prize in Physics twice — in 1956 for the invention of the transistor and in 1972 for the BCS theory of superconductivity.
Persons to win a Nobel Prize twice: Marie Curie (first ever), Linus Pauling, Frederick Sanger, John Bardeen, and K Barry Sharpless (most recent, 2022).
Electricity is Benjamin Franklin; Telephone - Alexander Graham Bell; Cell phone - Martin Cooper (Motorola).
Television is John Logie Baird; Steam Engine - Thomas Newcomen, improved by James Watt; Penicillin - Alexander Fleming.
Thermometer is Gabriel Fahrenheit; Battery - Alessandro Volta; Airplane - Wright Brothers.
Oxygen is Joseph Priestley; Radio - Guglielmo Marconi; Electric Bulb - Thomas Edison.
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was formed in 1981 in Riyadh among Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates for regional economic and political cooperation.

The UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change) was established in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 and ratified by 197 countries. Nations meet annually at the Conference of Parties (COP) to review climate progress.
The Glasgow Climate Pact (COP26, 2021) was the first climate agreement to explicitly commit to reducing unabated coal usage and included a pledge to phase down coal.

The Paris Agreement (COP21, 2015) aims to keep global temperature rise well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, preferably limiting it to 1.5°C. Emissions must reach net-zero by the middle of the 21st century.

COP27 took place in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt in November 2022 under the theme 'Together for Implementation'. It established a landmark Loss and Damage fund for vulnerable countries affected by climate change.

QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) comprises the United States, Australia, India, and Japan. It was formed to promote a free, open, prosperous, and inclusive Indo-Pacific region and has no physical headquarters.

G20 (Group of 20) is an intergovernmental forum comprising 19 countries and the EU, representing 85% of global GDP, 75% of global trade, and 66% of global population. India held the G20 presidency in 2022–23 with the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'.

G7 (International Group of Seven) consists of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States, plus the European Union as a non-enumerated member. It focuses on trade, security, economics, and climate change.
BRICS is an acronym for five major emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. India chairs the 18th BRICS summit, to be held in September 2026.
The New Development Bank (formerly BRICS Development Bank) was established by the BRICS states in 2015 and is headquartered in Shanghai, China. President - Dilma Rousseff.

NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is an intergovernmental military alliance of 31 member states formed in 1949. Its headquarters are in Brussels, Belgium. Secretary General - Jens Stoltenberg.

AIIB (Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank) is the world's second-largest multilateral development institution with 106 members. India holds a 7.6% stake. Headquarters - Beijing, China. President - Jin Liqun; VP - Dr Urjit Patel.

SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) is the world's largest regional organization by geographic scope and population. India and Pakistan joined on 9 June 2017. Headquarters - Beijing; Secretary General - Zhang Ming.
SCO is the only plurilateral grouping with a dedicated counterterrorism body — RATS (Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure) — which addresses terrorism, separatism, and religious extremism.

The Raisina Dialogue is India's flagship annual multilateral conference on geopolitics and geo-economics, hosted in New Delhi by the Observer Research Foundation in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs.

ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is a political and economic union of 10 Southeast Asian states. Founding members: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Headquarters - Jakarta, Indonesia.

RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) is a free trade agreement between 10 ASEAN members and Australia, China, Japan, South Korea, and New Zealand. India pulled out of negotiations in November 2019.

MTCR (Missile Technology Control Regime) is a multilateral export control regime started in 1987 by G7 countries to limit missile technology proliferation. India became a member in 2016. Total members - 35.
AUKUS is a trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States for the Indo-Pacific region, signed in 2021.

IORA (Indian Ocean Rim Association) is an inter-governmental organisation with 23 Member States and 10 Dialogue Partners, aimed at regional cooperation in the Indian Ocean. Headquartered in Ebene, Mauritius. Founded by India and South Africa.

OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) was created in Baghdad in 1960. It has 13 members and is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. Secretary General - Haitham Al Ghais. OPEC+ includes 10 additional non-OPEC oil exporters.
SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) has 8 member states: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal.
The G4 nations — Brazil, Germany, India, and Japan — support each other's bids for permanent seats on the UN Security Council. Founded in 2005.

OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation) is the second-largest intergovernmental organisation after the UN, with 57 member states. India is not a member. Founded September 1969 in Rabat, Morocco. Headquarters - Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

ADB (Asian Development Bank) envisions a prosperous, inclusive, resilient Asia. It has 68 members and is headquartered in Manila, Philippines. Largest shareholders: USA and Japan (15.6% each), China (6.4%), India (6.3%).
OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) has 38 member countries and is headquartered in Paris, France. India is not a member. Secretary General - Mathias Cormann.
I2U2 is a grouping of India, Israel, UAE, and the United States formed to cooperate on water, energy, transportation, space, health, and food security.

The Wassenaar Arrangement (1996) is a voluntary export control regime with 42 members that regulates transfers of conventional weapons and dual-use technologies. India joined in 2017 and assumed the chairmanship in January 2023. Headquarters - Vienna, Austria.

IBSA Dialogue Forum is an international tripartite group for cooperation among India, Brazil, and South Africa — three large democracies from three different continents. It has no permanent headquarters.

FATF (Financial Action Task Force) was set up in 1989 at the G7 summit in Paris to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. It meets three times a year. Countries on its blacklist include North Korea, Iran, and Myanmar.

WEF (World Economic Forum) is an international NGO and think tank founded by Klaus Schwab on 24 January 1971, based in Cologny, Geneva. It publishes the Global Gender Gap Index. President and CEO - Børge Brende. India ranked 131 out of 148 in 2025.

Pax Silica is a US-led international coalition to build a secure silicon and AI supply chain ecosystem. India joined at the AI Impact Summit 2026. Other signatories include Canada, Japan, South Korea, and the European Union.

The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco and came into force on 24 October 1945. The UN has 193 member states. The six principal organs are: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, and the Secretariat.

The UN Security Council has 5 permanent members (P5) — China, France, Russia, UK, and USA — each with veto power. 10 non-permanent members are elected for two-year terms. India has been elected to the UNSC eight times.
UN Secretary-General (9th) - António Guterres. FAO Director General - Qu Dongyu (Rome). ILO Director General - Gilbert Houngbo (Geneva). WHO Director General - Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Geneva).

IMF (International Monetary Fund) has 190 member countries and is headquartered in Washington DC. Managing Director - Kristalina Georgieva; First Deputy MD - Gita Gopinath; Chief Economist - Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas.

World Bank President - Ajay Banga (first Indian-American WB President). The World Bank operates in over 100 countries and is headquartered in Washington DC. It comprises IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID.

UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) is headquartered in Paris, France. Director General - Audrey Azoulay. It focuses on education, culture, and the protection of world heritage sites.
WTO (World Trade Organization) Director General - Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Headquarters - Geneva, Switzerland. UNHCR High Commissioner - Filippo Grandi. IAEA Director General - Rafael Grossi (Vienna).

India has 7 Nuclear Power Plants with 22 reactors, operated by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL). India's nuclear power is the fourth-largest electricity source after thermal, hydroelectric, and renewable sources.

India's nuclear power plants: Tarapur (oldest, 1969, Maharashtra), Rajasthan (1973), Madras/Kalpakkam (1984, Tamil Nadu), Narora (1991, UP), Kakrapar (1993, Gujarat), Kaiga (2000, Karnataka), Kudankulam (largest, 2013, Tamil Nadu).
India's FTA with the UAE (CEPA) and Australia (ECTA) were both signed in 2022. The India-EU FTA came into force in 2026. India-Sri Lanka FTA (ISLFTA) was implemented in 2000.

FTA types: FTA reduces tariffs; CEPA is comprehensive (goods, services, investment); CECA focuses on tariffs and quotas; PTA grants reductions on selected goods; EHS offers fast-track early tariff cuts; ECTA is a modern comprehensive pact.

Booker Prize winners from India: VS Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006), and Aravind Adiga (2008). Man Booker Prize 2022 - The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida by Shehan Karunatilaka.
The International Booker Prize 2022 - Tomb of Sand by Geetanjali Shree (translated from Hindi Ret Samadhi by Daisy Rockwell), the first Hindi novel to win the International Booker Prize.

Pulitzer Prize for Fiction 2022 - The Netanyahus by Joshua Cohen; 2023 - Trust by Hernan Diaz and Demon Copperhead by Barbara Kingsolver. Reuters photographers including Danish Siddiqui won the 2022 Pulitzer for Covid-19 coverage in India.

Jnanpith Award is the oldest and highest Indian literary award, given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith. It is bestowed on Indian writers for works in Indian languages. Winner in 2022 - Damodar Mauzo (Konkani).

China's String of Pearls strategy refers to a network of Chinese military and commercial facilities along sea routes — including in Pakistan (Gwadar), Sri Lanka (Hambantota), Bangladesh (Chittagong), Myanmar (Coco Islands), Maldives, and Djibouti.

India counters China's String of Pearls with its Necklace of Diamonds strategy, including the Act East Policy, QUAD, Chabahar port in Iran, and naval access agreements with Seychelles, Oman, Singapore, and France.

Debt-trap diplomacy refers to China's practice of extending loans with unfavourable terms that increase its political leverage over borrowing nations. Sri Lanka's Hambantota Port was leased to China for 99 years in 2017 after failing to repay debt.
ICC Chairman is Greg Barclay; ICC CEO - Geoff Allardice; BCCI President - Roger Binny; BCCI Secretary - Jay Shah; FIFA President - Gianni Infantino.
Joe Root became the first England player to complete 17,000 runs in international cricket.
Indian cricketer Mithali Raj retired from all forms of cricket on June 8, 2022.
Rafael Nadal won the men's singles final at Roland Garros 2022 (French Open).
Carlos Alcaraz defeated Casper Ruud to win the US Open 2022, becoming the youngest ATP World No. 1.
Sharath Kamal Achanta was awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award 2022 for his achievements in Table Tennis.
Shubman Gill became the youngest batter to hit a double hundred in ODI cricket history and the fastest Indian batter to reach 4 ODI centuries, in just 21 innings.
Renuka Singh Thakur became the first Indian to win the ICC Emerging Women's Cricketer of the Year award.
Aryna Sabalenka (Belarus) won the Australian Open 2023 Women's singles title, defeating Elena Rybakina (Kazakhstan).
Novak Djokovic (Serbia) won his 10th Australian Open Men's singles title in 2023, defeating Stefanos Tsitsipas (Greece).
India won its first women's ICC tournament by clinching the inaugural U19 T20 World Cup, defeating England. Captain - Shafali Verma; Top scorer - Shweta Sehrawat.
Germany beat Belgium to win the Men's Hockey World Cup 2023, held in Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha. Netherlands finished third; India finished ninth. President of Hockey India - Dilip Tirkey.
Sania Mirza retired from professional tennis after a 20-year career. She is the first and only Indian woman to win a Grand Slam title, having won 6 Grand Slams and 43 WTA doubles titles.

MGNREGA is Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.

MGNREGA is one of the largest work guarantee programmes in the world launched in 2005 by the Ministry of Rural development. The primary objective of the scheme is to guarantee 100 days of employment in every financial year to adult members of any rural household willing to do public work-related unskilled manual work.
As of 2022-23, there are 15.4 crore active workers under the MGNREGA.
MGNREGA’s role and importance was very prominent during the Corona period.

The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 - VBG RAM-G represents a major overhaul of MNREGA. Under the proposed law, the government "establishes a modern statutory framework aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047, guaranteeing 125 days of guaranteed work, an increase from the earlier mandate of 100 days. In addition, the minimum daily wage has been revised to Rs 240, offering improved income support for workers dependent on the scheme.

VBG RAM-G: Legal right to work - Unlike earlier employment guarantee schemes, the act aims at addressing the causes of chronic poverty through a rights-based framework. At least one-third of beneficiaries have to be women.

VBG RAM-G: Demand driven scheme - The most important part of MGNREGA’s design is its legally-backed guarantee for any rural adult to get work within 15 days of demanding it, failing which an ‘unemployment allowance’ must be given.

Decentralized planning - There is an emphasis on strengthening the process of decentralization by giving a significant role to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in planning and implementing these works. The act mandates Gram sabhas to recommend the works that are to be undertaken and at least 50% of the works must be executed by them.

VBG RAM-G Challenges: Delay and Insufficiency in Funds Dispersal: Most states have failed to disburse wages within 15 days as mandated by MGNREGA. In addition, workers are not compensated for a delay in payment of wages. This has turned the scheme into a supply-based programme and subsequently, workers had begun to lose interest in working under it.

VBG RAM-G Challenges: Caste Based Segregation: There were significant variations in delays by caste. While 46% of payments to SC workers and 37% for ST workers were completed in the mandated seven-day period, it was a dismal 26% for non-SC/ST workers. The negative impact of caste-based segregation was felt acutely in poorer States such as Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.
VBG RAM-G Challenges: Ineffective Role of PRI: With very little autonomy, gram panchayats are not able to implement this act in an effective and efficient manner.

VBG RAM-G Challenges: Large Number of Incomplete works: There has been a delay in the completion of works under MGNREGA and inspection of projects has been irregular. Also, there is an issue of quality of work and asset creation under MGNREGA.

VBG RAM-G Challenges: March 16 - In the budget of financial year 23-24, released on Feb 1, 2023, the Budget Estimate for MGNREGS was reduced to 29,400 crore or 33% compared to the estimate of 22-23. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Rural Development questioned this reduced allocation and expressed distress over the delay in wage payments and material fund release to State governments. It flagged the chronic problem of non-adherence to the provision of delay compensation.

Piezoelectric Effect is the ability of certain materials to generate an electric charge in response to applied mechanical stress or pressure. This effect occurs when the material is subjected to a force that causes its molecules to become polarized, i.e the +ve and -ve charges are separated from each other. When this polarization occurs, an electric potential is generated across the material, and if the material is connected to the circuit, a current can flow.
Piezoelectric materials are used in sensors, actuators, and energy harvesting devices. Ex - quartz, ceramics and certain types of crystals.

Scientists spot piezoelectric effect in liquids for the first time. The effect has been known for 143 years and in this time has been observed only in solids. The new finding challenges the theory that describes this effect as well as opens the door to previously unanticipated applications in electronic and mechanical systems.

The Artemis programme is a series of ongoing space missions run by NASA.
Three Artemis missions are currently in progress:.

Artemis 1, an uncrewed test flight completed on 11 December 2022 which circled and flew past the Moon. Artemis 1 also carried two very special passengers in Shaun the Sheep and Snoopy. This uncrewed mission was an extensive test of the Space Launch System (SLS) and the Orion module. The Space Launch System is the most powerful rocket ever built, generating 8.8 million pounds of thrust on liftoff, making it 1.3 million pounds more powerful than the Saturn V rocket used in the Apollo missions.

Artemis 2, a crewed flight beyond the Moon, which will take humans the furthest they’ve ever been in space. After being launched into space by the SLS rocket, the four-person crew will fly the Orion module 7402 km beyond the far side of the Moon, complete a lunar flyby and return to Earth. The mission will take between eight to ten days and collect valuable flight test data. Currently planned to be launched in Nov 2024.
Artemis 2’s crew were announced on 3 April 2023. They are: Christina Koch, mission specialist; Jeremy Hansen, mission specialist; Reid Wiseman, commander; and Victor Glover, pilot.
Artemis 3, which will land the first female astronaut and first astronaut of color on the Moon, and involve spending a week performing scientific studies on the lunar surface.

Artemis 3 will be the US space agency's first crewed Moon landing mission since Apollo 17 in 1972. The astronauts are expected to spend a week exploring the surface and perform a variety of scientific studies, including sampling water ice - first detected on the Moon in 1971.
Key NASA mission objective - Equality: a chief aim for NASA is to land the first woman and first person of colour on the lunar surface.
Key NASA mission objective -Technology: from rockets to spacesuits, the technologies currently being developed are designed to pave the way for future deep-space missions.
Key NASA mission objective - Partnerships: the Artemis programme is one of NASA's first large-scale collaborations with commercial companies, such as SpaceX and Boeing.
Key NASA mission objective - Long-term presence: where the Apollo 17 crew spent three days on the lunar surface, Artemis aims to establish a base to extend the trips to weeks and possibly months.

Key NASA mission objective - Knowledge: as more is known about the Moon compared with 50 years ago (and technologies have greatly advanced), NASA claims that this next series of missions will be able to retrieve samples more strategically than during the Apollo era.
Key NASA mission objective - Resources: the discovery of water on the Moon and potential deposits of rare minerals hold promise for both scientific and economic exploration and exploitation.

Debt-trap diplomacy is an international financial relationship where a creditor country or institution extends debt to a borrowing nation partially, or solely, to increase the lender's political leverage.

CHINA’S DEBT TRAP POLICY - The loans which China extends have never been very benign in nature and have been accompanied by major geopolitical leverage. China has faced criticism for its lending practices to poorer countries, accused of leaving them struggling to repay debts and therefore vulnerable to pressure from Beijing. China is one of the world's largest single creditor nations.

In accordance with investing $1 trillion for China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), 2013, China gives loans but on the condition that the contract is given to Chinese companies only - so Chinese laborers go to the country to work on the project. Hence, the loan that China gives gets circulated in the form of payment to Chinese workers back to China only. If a project is successful or fails, China benefits both ways. If a project fails and a country is not able to repay, China takes over the fai.

The most recent and prominent example of Deb Trap Policy leverage being Sri Lanka and the outcome of the Hambantota Port which is leased to China for a period of 99 years and 70 percent stakes, in 2017. The lease has a clause which calls for an extension by another 99 years if the loans are not paid. The lease provides Beijing with access and foothold in South Asia, and a docking space for its submarines and warships.

STRING OF PEARLS STRATEGY - A geopolitical theory related to potential Chinese intentions in the Indian Ocean region. It refers to the network of Chinese military and commercial facilities and relationships along its sea lines of communication - each pearl represents some form of permanent Chinese military installation in a series of locations along a string.

Sri Lanka: China took over Sri Lanka’s Hambantota port to firm up its naval operations in the Indian Ocean after the latter failed to repay the loan debt. China has also proposed setting up a radar base in the jungles near Dondra Bay in Sri Lanka, aiming to counter India's naval presence and strategic oversight in the Indian Ocean region.
Bangladesh: China made its presence in this country as well by setting up its naval base at Chittagong Port.

Problems with Stubble burning - 1) Pollution and greenhouse gas emissions that lead to global warming: These directly contribute to environmental pollution and are also responsible for the haze in Delhi and melting of Himalayan glaciers.

Problems with Stubble burning - 2) Soil degradation is another problem due to burning of crop residues. Burning paddy straw radiates heat that kills fungus and bacteria that is essential for soil fertility.

Problems with Stubble burning - 3) The pollutants dispersed due to stubble burning in the atmosphere eventually affect air quality and people’s health by forming a thick blanket of smog. The smoke apart from causing irritation to eyes, also lead to breathing difficulties and lung diseases.

Solutions for stubble burning - (i) Innovative farm technologies:To reduce manual costs, as well as save labor and time, new innovative farm technologies have been introduced by the government. One of the recent innovations that could help farmers to manage crop residues effectively is by employing agricultural machines like Happy seeder, Rotavator, Paddy straw chopper etc. But these machines are too costly. Therefore, the government could provide adequate subsidies to make this machinery affordable for farmers.

Solutions for stubble burning - (ii) Another possible solution is to use Pusa-bio-decomposer, developed by the scientists at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, which turns crop residue to manure in 15-20 days by accelerating the decomposition process.

Solutions for stubble burning - (iii) Biogas plants can curb crop burning and prevent pollution. These plants are installed by the government under the ‘waste to energy mission’ and they generate biogas by utilizing crop waste such as rice straw through bio-methanation technology.

Solutions for stubble burning - (iv) Sustainable farm management practices: Other measures suggested by agriculturists and scientists include composting, production of biochar, in-situ management with mechanical intensification. These measures could not only manage the crop residues but could also help in controlling GHG emissions.

Solutions for stubble burning - (v) Educating and empowering the stakeholders: Educating and empowering the farming community could be an important step to make a significant impact. Farmers feel that they are responsible only for growing foodgrains and the crop residue is not their responsibility. This thinking should be changed and farmers should feel responsible for crop residues and this should be brought through awareness campaigns.

Solutions for stubble burning - (vi) The government should act as an enabler by spreading awareness about the pros and cons of each option, so as to eliminate confusion and ease the adoption of new technologies by removing socio-economic barriers so that these new and innovative technologies can be accessed by small and marginal farmers.

UPI - The future of digital payments - Unified Payments Interface, is an instant real-time payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). The National Payments Corporation of India, an umbrella organization for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India, is an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Indian Banks’ Association (IBA).
UPI works through IMPS (Immediate Payment System) for smartphones using Virtual Private Address(VPS) or AePS (Aadhar enabled payment system) for PoS systems using Aadhar number and fingerprint scan.

In Oct 2021, UPI crossed $100 billion in transactions. In December 2022, UPI crossed 7.82 billion transactions worth Rs 12.82 trillion. UPI-based transactions grew in value (121%) and volume (115%) terms, between 2019-22, paving the way for its international adoption.
